title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Explore the commercial corridors and historic streets that define student life in Providence's East Side and Jewelry District.

cards.title: The Student Commercial Hub
cards.subtitle: Thayer Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this primary commercial strip to visit the Brown Bookstore or grab a quick meal at local favorites like East Side Pockets.
cards.short_summary: Thayer Street is the central commercial artery for Brown students, featuring a dense mix of independent shops and global eateries.
cards.evidence_claim: Thayer Street is described as the heart of the Brown University neighborhood, catering to the college crowd with dozens of unique businesses.
cards.source_title: Brown ❤️ Providence campaign launching Feb. 14 | Office of the President
cards.access_notes: Public street with high pedestrian activity; most businesses open late to accommodate student schedules.

cards.title: Fox Point's Eclectic Strip
cards.subtitle: Wickenden Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore this historic street in Fox Point for independent art galleries, coffee houses, and unique vintage finds.
cards.short_summary: Wickenden Street offers a bohemian atmosphere with a mix of Portuguese heritage and modern student-friendly cafes.
cards.evidence_claim: Wickenden Street is a popular destination for students, featuring numerous independent shops, art galleries, and restaurants.
cards.source_title: Living in Providence | Watson School of International and Public Affairs - Brown University
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare located south of the main campus in the Fox Point neighborhood.

cards.title: The Creative Arts Corridor
cards.subtitle: Angell Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the Granoff Center for the Creative Arts or the Lindemann Performing Arts Center along this major campus-adjacent street.
cards.short_summary: Angell Street serves as a major east-west thoroughfare housing several of Brown's premier arts and research facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lindemann Performing Arts Center and Granoff Center are located along Angell Street, featuring public outdoor communal spaces.
cards.access_notes: Public street; outdoor seating at the Lindemann Tribune is available for public use.

cards.title: The Campus Gateway
cards.subtitle: Waterman Street Corridor
cards.notes: Access the Stephen Robert '62 Campus Center and the Watson Center for Information Technology on this central street.
cards.short_summary: Waterman Street is a primary campus artery connecting the Main Green to the eastern residential and academic quads.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stephen Robert '62 Campus Center is located at 75 Waterman Street, serving as a hub for student activities.
cards.source_title: Contact Us - Student Activities | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Public street; the Campus Center is open to students and visitors during academic hours.

cards.title: The Riverfront Connection
cards.subtitle: South Main Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk along the Providence River to reach the Jewelry District and the Warren Alpert Medical School facilities.
cards.short_summary: South Main Street connects the historic College Hill area to the modern research hubs in the Jewelry District.
cards.evidence_claim: Brown has invested significantly in the Jewelry District, with facilities like the Medical School located near South Main Street.
cards.source_title: Brown purchases its portion of South Street Landing in Providence's Jewelry District
cards.access_notes: Public street with pedestrian walkways along the riverfront.

cards.title: Upscale East Side Dining
cards.subtitle: Wayland Square Corridor
cards.notes: Visit this neighborhood square for a quieter study spot at local bakeries or to browse independent bookstores.
cards.short_summary: Wayland Square is a sophisticated shopping and dining district located a short walk east of the main campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Wayland Square is identified as a walkable neighborhood near Brown with international food markets and boutiques.
cards.source_title: Providence and Rhode Island - Global Brown Center
cards.access_notes: Public commercial district; easily accessible via the RIPTA bus or a 15-minute walk from campus.

cards.title: The Local Neighborhood Strip
cards.subtitle: Hope Street Corridor
cards.notes: Head north to find local specialty markets and community-focused businesses supported by the Brown community.
cards.short_summary: Hope Street offers a residential-commercial mix with local grocery stores and small businesses popular with graduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope Street is highlighted as a key area for local spending and community support through the 'Brown Loves Providence' initiative.
cards.source_title: Through 'Brown Loves Providence,' Brown community members turn appreciation into action
cards.access_notes: Public street; northern sections feature a high concentration of local shops and eateries.

cards.title: The Residential Spine
cards.subtitle: Brook Street Corridor
cards.notes: See the new student housing developments and access the Nelson Fitness Center along this north-south street.
cards.short_summary: Brook Street serves as a primary residential corridor, housing many of Brown's newest dormitory projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Brown has constructed new on-campus housing on both sides of Brook Street between Charlesfield and Power Streets.
cards.source_title: Brook Street Residence Halls - Facilities and Campus Operations
cards.access_notes: Public street; residential buildings require card access for entry.

cards.title: The Mile of History
cards.subtitle: Benefit Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this historic street to see one of the highest concentrations of Colonial architecture in the United States.
cards.short_summary: Benefit Street is a world-renowned historic district featuring beautifully preserved 18th and 19th-century homes.
cards.evidence_claim: Benefit Street is a designated historic district known for its architectural significance and proximity to the RISD Museum.
cards.access_notes: Public street; ideal for architectural walking tours.

cards.title: The Innovation Corridor
cards.subtitle: Eddy Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit South Street Landing or the Rhode Island Nursing Education Center in this rapidly developing district.
cards.short_summary: Eddy Street is the backbone of the Jewelry District, housing administrative offices and professional schools.
cards.evidence_claim: South Street Landing, located at 350 Eddy Street, is a $220 million redevelopment project housing Brown administrative offices.
cards.access_notes: Public street; South Street Landing lobby is accessible to visitors with proper identification.
